bug_semantics: TagReference.create() accepted caller-controlled path/reference positionals and passed them directly as (path, reference) to repo.git.tag() without an option terminator or unsafe-option inspection. A reference such as --file=/secret was therefore parsed by git tag as its file-input option, and GitPython returned the file contents through the annotated tag message. The later kwargs-only guard inspected Git._option_candidates([], kwargs), so it still omitted both vulnerable positional values.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable forwarding sink was first implemented in 1047b41e2e925617474e2e7c9927314f71ce7365: it replaced TagReference.create()'s NotImplementedError with args = (path, ref) followed by repo.git.tag(*args, **kwargs). Commit 3af0c2516c5e18c829da30338614688f6b69b49c was a later incomplete mitigation, not the origin: it added a --file/-F denylist but passed an empty positional list to the checker. Historical moves and formatting commits preserved the 2009 sink and are not BICs.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p 1047b41e2e925617474e2e7c9927314f71ce7365 shows author and committer Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com> and a two-line message with no Co-Authored-By, Assisted-by, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-3wxw-xv34-2frg identifies the reference=--file=<path> attack, the in-band tag.message disclosure, affected GitPython <=3.1.58, patched >=3.1.59, and the incomplete kwargs-only guard from 3af0c251.

git log -L 90,165:git/refs/tag.py at 3af0c251 traced the surviving create() sink through formatting and the dec4663129f72321a14efd6de63f14a7419e3ed2 file split; git log -S 'repo.git.tag(*args, **kwargs)' --all located the earlier implementation commit 1047b41e2e925617474e2e7c9927314f71ce7365, showing the split was only a move.

git show 1047b41e2e925617474e2e7c9927314f71ce7365 -- lib/git/refs.py shows the exact causal change: parent code raised NotImplementedError, while the commit added args = (path, ref) and repo.git.tag(*args, **kwargs). git rev-parse 1047b41e2e925617474e2e7c9927314f71ce7365^ returned ddc5496506f0484e4f1331261aa8782c7e606bf2; the parent-side diff contains no executable tag call, directly verifying immediate-parent absence.

git show 3af0c2516c5e18c829da30338614688f6b69b49c -- git/refs/tag.py shows the incomplete mitigation's Git._option_candidates([], kwargs), while path and reference remained in args = (path, reference) for repo.git.tag().

git show 1b0d2d9b91575f7db44ef4ff58ac37fc9335e5f6 -- git/refs/tag.py shows the direct fix changing the candidates to [path, reference], resolving the ref alias before checking, and adding positional --file/-F regression cases.

Version ancestry: tag 3.1.58 resolves to 30be45d786e95023e23c616fec5cbabca861b44c and contains the BIC but not the fix; tag 3.1.59 resolves to 66340d77aab9a7468f4aed3681d4ef1e3c0ec931 and contains 1b0d2d9b91575f7db44ef4ff58ac37fc9335e5f6. git tag --contains the BIC begins at 0.2.0-beta1, consistent with the advisory's no-lower-bound <=3.1.58 affected range.
BIC-only AI check: raw commit object 1047b41e2e925617474e2e7c9927314f71ce7365 has one parent, human author/committer Sebastian Thiel, and no trailers or AI disclosure.
reasoning: The vulnerability starts with the first working TagReference.create() implementation, not with the 2026 attempted mitigation. Commit 1047b41e2e925617474e2e7c9927314f71ce7365 made both tag-name path and target ref positional argv elements and invoked git tag without '--'; its immediate parent only had a NotImplementedError, so the exploitable sink is absent there. History tracing shows dec4663129f72321a14efd6de63f14a7419e3ed2 merely split the file and subsequent edits preserved the same sink. Commit 3af0c2516c5e18c829da30338614688f6b69b49c added protection for kwargs but explicitly supplied [] as the positional candidate set, leaving reference=--file=<path> exploitable; that is an incomplete fix, not the smallest origin. Commit 1b0d2d9b91575f7db44ef4ff58ac37fc9335e5f6 directly closes the bypass by checking [path, reference] and is present in patched tag 3.1.59 but absent from vulnerable tag 3.1.58. The smallest BIC is a normal one-parent 2009 human commit whose raw commit object has no AI signal, so later AI-associated work cannot change the BIC-only verdict: NOT_AI.
